methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort of 130 nasopharyngeal carcinoma survivors with RCN, with 7:3 random split (n=91 training, n=39 testing). Radiomic feature extraction from 3D T2WI volumes, LASSO Cox regression for feature selection, multivariable Cox with backward stepwise selection, and integrated nomogram development are appropriate for prediction model development. Discriminative performance (C-index 0.841/0.867), time-ROC AUCs, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis are all reported. Variance inflation factor was checked (1.057). The single-center retrospective design and modest testing cohort (n=39) limit rigor, and the authors acknowledge that patients without follow-up MRI exclusion may bias survival estimates.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual prognostic/prediction cohort study with internal validation in a narrowly defined clinical problem (cerebral herniation in RCN after NPC radiotherapy), consistent with Oxford LoE 2b. The model addresses a high-stakes clinical decision (surveillance interval, surgical timing), and if externally validated could directly inform management of nasopharyngeal carcinoma survivors with RCN. Authors make concrete practice recommendations (3-month vs 6-month imaging intervals) that are clinically actionable.

reporting_quality.justification: As a multivariable prediction-model study, TRIPOD is the applicable standard, and reference 40 (Collins et al. TRIPOD statement) is cited, suggesting awareness. Methods are thoroughly described with a patient-flow supplement (Figure S1), a clear endpoint definition with supporting Methods S3, radiomic feature table (Table S3), and individualized risk-score formula. Calibration curves, decision curves, and subgroup analyses are all reported. However, explicit TRIPOD checklist adherence is not declared, no data/code repository is provided despite being a reproducibility-critical radiomics paper, and only internal validation was performed.

novelty_literature.justification: This is described as the first radiomic model specifically predicting cerebral herniation in RCN among NPC survivors. The authors previously published related work (ref 19 — radiomic prediction of cystic brain radionecrosis itself; ref 18 and 25 — radiomic models for bevacizumab/methylprednisolone response), so the contribution is a natural extension of an established radiomics program into a new clinical endpoint (herniation). Meaningful but incremental.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized and clear, with a logical workflow (Figure 1), thoroughly described methods, appropriate figure/table references, and transparent limitations. The clinical recommendations are concrete and grounded in model-derived risk strata. Writing is polished with only minor stylistic issues.

key_strengths: Strong prediction-model workflow: LASSO Cox feature selection, multivariable backward-stepwise selection, integrated nomogram, internal validation with C-index 0.841/0.867
Comprehensive performance evaluation including time-ROC, calibration curves, decision-curve analysis, and subgroup analyses
Clinically actionable risk thresholds and concrete surveillance recommendations (3-month vs 6-month imaging)
Awareness of TRIPOD framework (cited) and appropriate selection of LASSO Cox for high-dimensional data
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with only internal validation (testing cohort n=39) — external multi-center validation is needed before clinical adoption
No data/code repository disclosed despite radiomics requiring reproducibility
Exclusion of patients without follow-up MRI likely overestimates herniation-free survival (acknowledged)
T2WI-only imaging limits multi-parametric characterization; no multi-sequence radiomics explored
TRIPOD checklist adherence not explicitly declared
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically sound internally-validated prediction model addressing a clinically important problem with actionable stratification, but requires external multi-center validation and explicit TRIPOD/reproducibility disclosures; plausible at tier 2 with major revisions, or tier 3 as-is.
